open_points.subject: installation.current_token_list retry after invalid configuration
open_points.text: “Re-read when the file's digest changed or it cannot be read; three checks only; a failed re-read leaves no list until one passes”
open_points.question: After a readable but invalid re-read, must every subsequent request retry validation even when the file bytes and digest have not changed, and which digest is retained as the comparison baseline?
options: Retain the last valid digest and retry while the invalid bytes differ
Retain the invalid digest and retry only after another file change
Retry on every request whenever there is no valid token list
open_points.default_guess: Retry on every request whenever there is no valid token list.

open_points.subject: agent-name uniqueness during token-list reload
open_points.text: “Exactly three checks apply to a re-read: the file can be read and parsed; every token is at least 43 characters; no two tokens are equal.” versus “names are unique in an installation, and a configuration repeating one is refused at start.”
open_points.question: May a live token-list reload introduce two agent tokens with the same agent name, and if not, is name uniqueness a fourth reload check despite the declared exact set of three?
options: Reject duplicate agent names on every reload
Permit duplicate names after start
Keep only one token for each repeated name
open_points.default_guess: Reject duplicate agent names on every reload.

open_points.subject: effects.decide_effect_approval refusal trace
open_points.text: “Inputs: An approval identity, approve or refuse, the actor (the owner); from runs that the run has not ended.” and “Outputs: The approval approved, or refused with the element's NodeExecution refused_by_owner.”
open_points.question: From where does effects obtain the exact StoredValue and SpooledFile references required for the refused_by_owner NodeExecution, given that the operation receives no element inputs and EffectApproval specifies input digests and a preview rather than trace input references?
options: EffectApproval persistently stores all trace input references
runs passes the element's trace input references to decide_effect_approval
effects reconstructs references from the preview and binding
open_points.default_guess: EffectApproval stores the exact trace input references needed by the later refusal record.

open_points.subject: effects.reach_operation_element input representation
open_points.text: “Inputs: The run's id, its pinned flow version, the FlowActivation under which it started, that it has not ended, the node and element, the input values by port, the actor.”
open_points.question: For each value and file input, does runs pass content bytes, StoredValue/SpooledFile references, or both, and which module reads file bytes and canonical value bytes before prepare_request?
options: Pass references and let effects read bytes from store
Pass fully resolved bytes and references from runs
Pass values as bytes but files as spool references
open_points.default_guess: Pass exact record references plus resolved bytes, so effects can write trace references while preparing the request.

open_points.subject: multipart request covered by an approval
open_points.text: “the fully built request as the owner was shown it — method, URL, headers and body. Any difference at send ... asks again” versus “the multipart/form-data content type without its boundary parameter” and “the boundary is not part of it: equal parts give equal descriptions.”
open_points.question: Is approval coverage byte-exact for multipart requests, including boundary-dependent body bytes and Content-Length, or is it deliberately semantic over the ordered parts with boundary differences ignored?
options: Cover exact wire bytes including a fixed boundary
Cover ordered multipart parts and ignore boundary-only differences
Cover parts but require a deterministic boundary without including it in the digest
open_points.default_guess: Use a deterministic boundary and exact serialization, while keeping the semantic part description as the approval digest input.

open_points.subject: multipart Content-Disposition names
open_points.text: “Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>", with filename="<port>" added for a file part”
open_points.question: What characters may a port name contain when inserted into quoted multipart header parameters, and how are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII characters and line breaks rejected or escaped?
options: Restrict port names to an ASCII token grammar
Define quoted-string escaping and UTF-8 handling
Percent-encode names in multipart parameters
open_points.default_guess: Restrict port names used in multipart requests to a safe ASCII token grammar.

open_points.subject: manifest api_base_url acceptance and joining
open_points.text: “one that is not an absolute http or https URL with a host counts as none” and “The URL is the api_base_url without a trailing / followed by the declared path.”
open_points.question: Are user information, a query, fragment, non-root path, multiple trailing slashes, percent-encoded host text, IPv6 zone identifiers and internationalized hosts allowed in api_base_url, and what exact authority string and joined URL result for each?
options: Allow only an origin URL consisting of scheme, host and optional port
Allow an existing base path but forbid user information, query and fragment
Accept every absolute HTTP URL and concatenate textually as stated
open_points.default_guess: Allow only scheme, host and optional port, with no user information, query, fragment or base path.

open_points.subject: manifest and required-header resource bounds
open_points.text: “its required_headers with their manifest values verbatim” and “Traces carry no secret and no unbounded payload.”
open_points.question: What limits apply to manifest file size, capability and instance counts, required-header count, names and values, and the approval preview/request description produced from them; what result occurs when a limit is exceeded?
options: Apply bounded_text_bytes_max and a release-defined manifest-size limit
Apply only transport or parser implementation limits
Treat an oversized manifest/header as binding_stale at send and manifest mismatch at proposal
open_points.default_guess: Apply explicit release limits and report manifest mismatch on proposal or acceptance, binding_stale on a later send.

open_points.subject: outbound service request size
open_points.text: “Build one request from a ManifestOperation and inputs” and the release ceiling table, which defines service_response_bytes_max but no service-request ceiling
open_points.question: Is there a maximum for the fully encoded URL, headers and body of an outbound request, including repeated references to large spooled files, and what pre-send result is returned if it is exceeded?
options: Add a release-fixed outbound request ceiling
Reuse surface_request_bytes_max
Stream without an additional encoded-request limit
open_points.default_guess: Stream the request without inventing an additional refusal, while retaining the existing per-value, per-file and per-run spool limits.

open_points.subject: service failure_detail representation
open_points.text: “at most failure_detail_bytes_max of it is kept as failure_detail” and “a classified failure_detail ... only as its length and that class”
open_points.question: How are arbitrary non-UTF-8 HTTP error-body bytes represented in failure_detail, where truncation occurs, and is the masked length a byte count, Unicode-scalar count or displayed-character count?
options: Decode UTF-8 with replacement and report encoded byte length
Store a bounded byte string and expose base64 plus byte length
Keep failure_detail only when valid UTF-8, otherwise omit it
open_points.default_guess: Store a UTF-8-decoded replacement-safe excerpt truncated by encoded bytes, and report its UTF-8 byte length.

open_points.subject: sandbox.probe_sandbox
open_points.text: “Check at start that bubblewrap is present and one probe execution succeeds.”
open_points.question: What exact code, inputs, bounds, expected output and isolation checks constitute the probe, and which sandbox outcomes count as the named start failure?
options: Run a fixed no-input function with a fixed expected output
Run separate positive and forbidden-action probes
Check only process creation and interpreter startup
open_points.default_guess: Run a release-fixed no-input function with fixed bounds and verify its exact successful output and cleanup.

open_points.subject: store.open_store privacy check
open_points.question: What exact ownership and permission modes are accepted for the data directory, database, value area, fixtures, spool directories and existing files, and does an absent directory get created or cause refusal?
options: Require owner-only permissions and correct ownership on every component
Require only that group and others have no write permission
Create missing paths with owner-only permissions and validate existing paths
open_points.default_guess: Create missing paths with owner-only permissions, then require the kernel user to own every component with no group or other permissions.

open_points.subject: runs.recover_running_runs spool-removal result
open_points.text: “Outputs: Done. Observable effect: Spools of ended runs that keep none are gone” versus “a spool that cannot be removed does not [stop the start]”
open_points.question: What does recovery report and guarantee when removal of an ended run's spool fails: successful recovery with bytes still present, an internal warning state, or a stopped start?
options: Continue startup and weaken the output guarantee to logically inaccessible spools
Stop startup on removal failure
Continue startup but persist a cleanup-needed record for retry
open_points.default_guess: Continue startup, keep the spool logically inaccessible, log the failure, and retry removal at the next start.

open_points.subject: functions.try_implementation persistence
open_points.text: “Observable effect: None.” versus “State impact: One record_trial_execution per case.”
open_points.question: Is a try operation's TrialExecution evidence durably observable through inspection and repair views, or is the evidence returned only to the caller without persistent state?
options: Persist every TrialExecution as stated by A04 and State impact
Return transient evidence only
Persist only failed trial executions
